name: Clavyz Login Security Lite
author: Vigitals

sections.description:
Clavyz Login Security Lite combines login-path management and user-level two-factor authentication (2FA) in one WordPress administration interface. Rather than focusing only on hiding the default login address, it adds a second verification step for participating accounts, recovery options, and controls for XML-RPC authentication.

Login address and access

  • Choose a custom login path from the plugin settings.
  • Restrict direct access to the standard wp-login.php address when a custom path is enabled.
  • Keep WordPress login, logout, and lost-password URLs aligned with the configured path.
  • Redirect logged-out visitors requesting the administration area to the configured sign-in address.
  • Reset the login path to its default from the plugin settings.

Two-factor authentication

  • Optional, per-user TOTP authentication using six-digit codes from compatible authenticator apps.
  • Set up an authenticator by scanning a QR code or entering the secret manually.
  • Confirm an authenticator code before 2FA is enabled.
  • Require a password and then a TOTP code or an unused recovery code during normal WordPress sign-in for users who enable 2FA.
  • Generate single-use recovery codes, displayed in full when 2FA is activated.
  • Encrypt stored TOTP secrets using PHP OpenSSL and WordPress site salts.
  • Limit repeated incorrect 2FA attempts and reject reuse of an already accepted TOTP time step.
  • Allow administrators to view enrolled users and reset their 2FA enrollment when necessary.
  • Provide a documented emergency 2FA bypass using a file placed on the server by an administrator with file access. This bypass affects the second factor only; a valid username and password are still required.

Additional protection and administration

  • Optionally disable XML-RPC authentication.
  • Manage login-path and XML-RPC settings from a dedicated WordPress admin screen.
  • Reset the plugin settings to their defaults.
  • Enable or disable your own 2FA from the WordPress user profile and 2FA setup screen.
  • Use the included German translations; English is the source language.

Clavyz Lite does not require an external authentication service for TOTP verification. You need a compatible authenticator app and PHP OpenSSL support to enable 2FA. Changing the login path is only one layer of protection and does not replace secure passwords, updates, or two-factor authentication.

Lite and Pro

The features described above are included in Clavyz Login Security Lite. The settings screen may also show features available only in Clavyz Pro; these are clearly marked as Pro and are not included in Lite.

Switching editions and retaining data

Deactivate the other edition before activating Lite. Lite never activates, deactivates, uninstalls or deletes another plugin. If another edition becomes active, Lite pauses its own login/security hooks and shows an administrator notice. Installed but inactive editions do not prevent Lite from running.

Saved options, encrypted TOTP secrets, recovery-code hashes and replay-protection metadata are retained when Lite is deactivated or deleted. Lite has no uninstall cleanup. Settings resets affect only Lite’s login-path and XML-RPC settings and preserve other saved fields. Explicit account-level 2FA disable/reset actions still remove that account’s enrollment after permission and nonce checks. Keep the WordPress salts unchanged to retain access to encrypted secrets. Compatibility with a particular Pro release should be tested with that release before switching.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the Clavyz Login Security Lite plugin and activate it in WordPress.
  2. Open the Clavyz settings page and, if desired, configure a custom login path and XML-RPC authentication protection.
  3. If you change the login path, test the new sign-in address in a private browser window before ending your current session.
  4. Open your WordPress user profile or the plugin’s 2FA setup page, scan the QR code with an authenticator app, and confirm the displayed code.
  5. Save the generated recovery codes securely. Each code works only once.
sections.faq:
Is Clavyz Lite just a plugin for hiding wp-login.php?

No. Alongside the custom login path, Lite includes optional TOTP two-factor authentication, single-use recovery codes, controls for XML-RPC authentication, 2FA attempt limiting, and administrator-assisted 2FA resets.

Is two-factor authentication mandatory for every user?

No. In Lite, users can opt in to 2FA for their own accounts.

Which authenticator apps can I use?

Use an app that supports standard time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) with SHA-1, six digits, and a 30-second interval.

What happens if I lose my authenticator device?

Sign in using an unused recovery code. An administrator can also reset the account’s 2FA enrollment. If all normal recovery methods are unavailable, an administrator with server file access can temporarily bypass 2FA by creating disable-2fa.txt in the plugin directory. Remove this file immediately after access is restored.

Does the plugin send my TOTP codes to an external service?

No. TOTP verification is performed by the plugin on the WordPress server.

Does a custom login path replace two-factor authentication?

No. A custom path changes the entry point; 2FA adds an independent verification step for enrolled users.

Can I disable XML-RPC authentication?

Yes. The plugin provides an option to block authentication through XML-RPC. Review compatibility with any tools that depend on XML-RPC authentication before enabling it.

Can I use WordPress application passwords?

Accounts protected by 2FA must use the normal WordPress login form for interactive sign-in. WordPress application passwords can be used for supported API authentication workflows.
sections.changelog:
2026.100.1

  • Detect active editions from WordPress plugin metadata instead of fixed plugin folders, including multisite activation checks.
  • Load Lite classes only when no conflicting edition is active; keep edition switching under administrator control.
  • Preserve additional saved option fields when resetting Lite settings or the login path.

  • Document edition switching and retained security data.

  • Completed edition switching, package documentation and translations.

  • Retained saved options and user data during manual edition changes.
  • Completed WordPress-managed asset loading and reviewed Plugin Check findings.
